questions: Is pain the main reason you need crutches and walk so cautiously?
Is the pain mainly in your groin or hip?
Is the pain present in both hips?
Did this problem begin suddenly?
Did it begin after a fall, accident, or other injury?
Do you have low-back or buttock pain?
Have you had low-back or buttock pain for more than three months?
Is your stiffness worse in the morning and lasting longer than 30 minutes?
Does the stiffness improve with exercise or movement?
Does the pain wake you during the second half of the night?
Have you had fever or chills?
Have you recently had an infection?
Have you lost weight unintentionally?
Do you have numbness or tingling in either leg?
Do you have weakness in either leg?
Have you recently developed difficulty controlling your bladder or bowel movements?
Do you have numbness around your genitals or anus?
Have you had pain, redness, or swelling in other joints?
Have you had a painful red eye or been diagnosed with uveitis?
Have you had psoriasis?
Have you had prolonged diarrhea or inflammatory bowel disease?
Have you ever been diagnosed with ankylosing spondylitis or another inflammatory arthritis?
Have you ever had hip surgery or a hip replacement?
Have you ever had tuberculosis, cancer, or an infection involving your bones or joints?

results: 1. Detailed bedside neurological examination, including gait with and without crutches, tandem and backward walking, Romberg testing, turning, pull test, limb coordination, muscle tone, power, reflexes, plantar responses, and sensory examination
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
sensory examination (pinprick, vibration, proprioception): normal
coordination examination (limb and truncal): normal
posture and pull test: normal
tandem gait: normal
walking backward: the slow, guarded, wide-based pattern PERSISTS
Romberg test, repeated with distraction: negative
muscle tone (spasticity, rigidity, paratonia): genuine axial and lower-limb rigidity on passive movement
MRC power in all four limbs: 5/5 throughout
2. Bedside assessment for functional gait signs, including gait variability with distraction or dual-tasking, incongruent weakness, and improvement with running or hopping
distractibility testing (complex motor task with the unaffected side): no change in the movement
Hoover sign / hip-abductor sign: negative
running: cannot run; the pattern does not normalise
gait with a distracting or automatic task (dancing, counting backwards): no change - the gait is not distractible
knee buckling / astasia-abasia on walking: not present

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Anti-GAD65–positive autoimmune stiff-person spectrum disorder (classic stiff-person syndrome with predominant axial and lower-limb rigidity)

1. Stiff-leg syndrome, an anti-GAD65–associated focal stiff-person variant  
2. Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus (PERM)  
3. Functional gait disorder coexisting with or mimicking an organic rigidity syndrome
